title: Lift a photo that hangs by one corner back up to its wire with one hand, and peg its free corner there with the other
instruction: The photo hangs from the wire by one peg. Peg its other top corner to the wire too.
context: Hanging photos, drawings and cards on a wire or string with clothes pegs is an everyday way to display them at home, in classrooms and shops, and the same squeeze-and-clip is how washing is pegged out. A print held by one corner swings down: here its free corner hangs 10 cm below the wire, and lifted and let go it swings straight back. A peg opens only while its handles are squeezed, so it takes one hand's whole grip from the basket to the wire. The instruction does not say so, but the job needs both arms: one lifts the print's hanging end back up to the wire and keeps it there while the other brings the open peg down so that its jaws pass either side of a 1.2 mm wire and a 0.3 mm print together, and lets go. A print pulled out of its first peg scores 0.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Wire: a 1.2 mm steel photo-display wire, taut between two brown wooden posts (2 cm square, 17.2 cm tall) 30 cm apart, running across the table along y at x 30, from y -15 to y 15, 16 cm above the table. Photo: a 127 x 89 mm print (beach scene) on 250 gsm photo paper, 0.3 mm thick, 2.8 g, its picture facing the robot, just in front of the wire. One peg holds it 5 mm in from its left end and 12 mm down from its top edge, at y 3 (layout A) or y 1.5 (layout B, environment variable PEG_LOT=B). Held by that one corner it hangs swung down 61 degrees: its free top corner 10.1 cm below the wire, its lowest corner 1.6 cm above the table. Hanging level it would reach 1.2 cm above the wire, its free end at y -9.2 (A) or y -10.7 (B). Pegs: three soft-grip wooden clothes pegs, 72 mm long, legs 5 x 10 mm, pivot 30 mm from the jaw tips, 6 g; a torsion spring (0.25 N m/rad, wound 7 degrees past shut) presses the tips together with about 1 N, and squeezed fully open (18 degrees, 10 mm between the tips) pushes back with about 5 N at the handles; a groove across each jaw for the line 5 to 14 mm up from its tip; handles splayed 8 degrees with green rubber grip pads. One peg holds the photo on the wire; two spares are clipped on the basket. Basket: a fixed blue plastic basket, 12 x 12 cm, rim 9 cm tall, walls 3 mm, its near wall along y at x 24 from y -30 to y -18, with the spare pegs on that wall's rim at y -22 and y -26, legs across the wall. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, a ruler and a protractor. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the photo comes off its first peg (its pegged corner 1 cm or more from where it hung). Otherwise 1.0 once, for 2 s, a second peg holds the photo's free top corner on the wire with everything let go: the peg let shut by its spring (jaws under 4 degrees open), the wire between its jaws, the photo's paper between its jaws with their tips pinching it on the sheet 2 mm or more inside its edges and within 2 cm of its free end, both grippers more than 4 cm from that peg and from the photo, the photo within 5 degrees of level, and the peg and the photo at rest (each moving less than 1 mm in 0.5 s). A peg on the wire beside the photo, or above a photo still hanging below it, does not count. Otherwise 0.25 for each of: a spare peg taken off the basket's rim (for 0.25 s the rim is no longer between its legs, and it has not dropped into the basket; squeezing it open on the rim or sliding it along the rim does not count); the photo's hanging end raised to the wire (the photo within 10 degrees of level for 1 s). Else 0.
reset_notes: Unclip the new peg and put it back on the basket's rim. Leave the photo held by its first peg at its left top corner, lightly enough that it swings down and hangs by that corner; if it came out, peg that corner again at the mark on the wire.
fidelity: Pegs, photo and wire are rigid. The second peg is fully simulated: two legs on a sprung pivot, opened by squeezing its handles, hanging on the wire by its jaws' groove and holding the print by friction at its tips. The first peg's hold is declared: a pivot the print turns freely in, bends up to 20 degrees out of plane against a light spring, and leaves at a 2 N pull (estimates). The spring (1 N at the tips) is lighter than most pegs'. A real wire sags a little.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right gripper hovered over the peg basket, then over the wire's right end; no peg taken, photo not lifted); demo: 1.0 (layout A, full score at step 488; layout B also 1.0). Videos: overhead, right wrist and left wrist cameras side by side.
